answer.rationale: Rollback is unavailable because the in-window release is a non-revertible security patch, so memory_b1 cannot be acted on. Circuit breaking is rejected: it fails requests and would drop customer writes, which violates the objective. Read-replica routing (memory_b5) recovered write latency only after offloading dashboard reads; the live symptom is heavy settlement writes, so replicas would not absorb the write peak. Regional failover (memory_b2) has restored latency before, but a cutover during peak settlement is an unneeded write-loss risk without regional evidence. Remaining write-safe lever is capacity: memory_b3 says headroom kept queue depth flat under surge. Timing mismatch remains (that add was before peak, this is mid-peak), so verify b3 and add capacity as a standard experiment—large enough to matter at 5x p99, not an unscoped broad rollout. Cause could still be the patch rather than load; capacity is the reversible availability move that does not discard writes.
